questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is in a crash, it should be:
questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been in a crash.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or sign. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Should be done to practice different riding situations.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle and changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to avoid riding alongside another vehicle.

questions.question: To lower crash risk, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others and make sure they understand your plans. Use proper signals and lane position. Keep enough space around you and scan ahead for hazards so you can react.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is best for normal riding, switch to single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front brake or only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should you ride to stay close while keeping a safe distance?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider safe space. Ride single-file when on curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if you need to avoid danger.
It makes it easier to talk to the other rider.
It makes it easier for other vehicles to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if you need to avoid danger.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle. This limits both riders' ways to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop. You need more space if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT needed for an effective eye or face shield?
questions.explanation: Good eye protection must be free of scratches, resistant to breaking, and fasten securely. It must allow air to flow through and fit over eyeglasses. It does NOT need to be airtight.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight. Extra weight means you need more braking power to stop. Stopping takes longer on downhill slopes than on flat roads.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection when riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection for riders.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They are caused by worn tires.
They occur at speeds above 55 mph.

questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen in daylight at low speeds.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, how does this affect acceleration and stopping?

options.text: Faster to accelerate, but slower to stop.
Slower to accelerate and slower to stop.
Slower to accelerate, but faster to stop.
Faster to accelerate and faster to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower to accelerate and slower to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes the motorcycle slower to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: Checking your motorcycle thoroughly:

options.text: Only works if a mechanic does it.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should only be done after a ride.
Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find problems that could be dangerous.

questions.question: For normal braking:

options.text: Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which option best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: Your body processes about one drink per hour. If someone drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks are likely in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Example: 7 drinks consumed in 3 hours, plus 3 more hours = 6 hours total. 7 drinks minus 6 hours = 1 drink processed. But the person had 7 drinks, so 4 drinks remain.

questions.question: A pre-ride check should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough check usually takes only a few minutes.
